changelog: **Security: only a super admin may set an organization's identity provider (#1575).** `PATCH /api/admin/organizations` let a tenant ADMIN write their own org's SAML provider, issuer, entry point and certificate. The ACS signs in any existing account of the org — any role — from an assertion checked only against that stored certificate, without a password or second factor, so a tenant admin of an org that also holds a super admin (the seeded operator lives in the default org) could paste a certificate they hold the key for and sign in as that super admin. Setting or changing those four fields is now super-admin only (`403 { code: 'sso_super_admin_only' }`, a `authz.scope_denied` warning); echoing the stored value back and clearing the config stay allowed, and the tenant ADMIN keeps the `ssoEnabled` switch and `ssoEnforced`. The admin SSO card locks the identity-provider inputs for a tenant admin with an explanation (EN/TR/DE). New `@smoke` e2e; `docs/sso-saml.md` § Who may set the identity provider.
